Lecturer/Senior Lecturer in Cybersecurity

Swansea

Job Ref
51756
Location
Swansea
Salary
£48,822 - £58,225 per annum
Closing Date
Friday, September 11, 2026

The University of Wales Trinity Saint David (UWTSD) traces its heritage back to the first university in Wales, receiving its Royal Charter in 1828 and is honoured to have His Majesty King Charles III as Royal Patron.
UWTSD now teaches over 16,000 students across its six campuses in the UK; four in Wales and two in England. It has long-standing international educational partnerships in Europe, China, Malaysia, the USA and elsewhere.
Our aim is to transform education, and by doing so transform the lives of the individuals and the communities we serve. We are already recognised for providing an outstanding student experience:
• 1st in Wales and 2nd in the UK for Student Satisfaction (Times Higher Education, July 2025)

Our success is due to the commitment, skill, knowledge, and ability of our people working together. We are now building on this strong culture and provision to become a leading provider of accessible higher education.

- THE ROLE –

The post of Senior Lecturer / Lecturer in Cybersecurity will be located within the Applied Computing team. The post holder will be under the line management of the Academic Director. The post holder is required to develop, manage and monitor undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, and requires in depth knowledge and skills in the areas of but not limited to, networks, cybersecurity, digital forensics, computer systems, Linux, OS, etc.
The post holder will deliver high-quality teaching in a variety of different learning environments and use a range of teaching styles and approaches, including all levels of undergraduate studies and, where appropriate, postgraduate studies. The post holder will be required to devise a range of teaching and assessment materials, covering several modules and subject areas.
The post holder will deliver teaching in a variety of different learning environments and use a variety of teaching styles and approaches, including all levels of undergraduate study and postgraduate study. The post holder will offer both academic and pastoral feedback and support to students to the highest professional standards and with regard to the ongoing enhancement of the student experience. Although we are a teaching-focused university, the post holder will be encouraged to undertake research that contributes to the Institute’s and University’s strategic priorities.

The post holder will undertake scholarship, research, training or project work, either individually or within a team, to ensure ongoing professional development and to enhance the profile of the Academic Discipline, Institute, and University. The post holder will make a positive contribution to the day-to-day activities of the academic discipline that may cover areas such as dissertation supervision, student recruitment, marketing activities, research seminars and workshops, staff training and professional development.

Please refer to the job descriptions for details on the essential criteria required for this role.

- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION -
- Annual leave entitlement is 35 days’, plus 8 bank holidays and 4 University closure days pro rata

- This post may be eligible for sponsorship

Interview date: TBC

- THE ROLE –
The post holder will be under the line management of the Academic Director and may be expected to take operational direction of the Therapy Assistant Practitioner Programme of Study at undergraduate level. Catering and Conference Assistant
Permanent, Part-time, 30 hours over 7 days
Grade 1 / £11.80 per hour. UWTSD is proud to be an Accredited Living Wage Employer. The Voluntary Living Wage (VLW) rate is £13.45 per hour. We will apply an adjustment to the rate of pay for this role to increase it to £13.45 per hour.

- THE ROLE -

Canolfan S4C Yr Egin is based at the University of Wales Trinity St David campus in Carmarthen and is a quality creative centre with a busy work environment. Since opening in 2018, Yr Egin's status has been established as a valuable resource for Carmarthen, Carmarthenshire and Wales.
Y Gegin, the café based on the ground floor, is an open and welcoming space and an important part of the vibrancy of the centre, and the Catering and Conference Assistant at Y Gegin will play an important role in maintaining the warm atmosphere of the café in order to attract and retain visitors to Yr Egin.

The post holder will be required to prepare specialist coffee and hot drinks, and serve high quality meals, delivering effective customer care that will complement the development of Yr Egin as a destination of choice in Carmarthen. Y Gegin has a wide customer base such as the creative community working at the centre, event audiences and University delegates, students and staff, as well as the local community, families and visitors, and therefore the Catering and Conference Assistant at Y Gegin will need to be able to communicate courteously and offer an experience that will urge the customer to return time after time.

Please refer to the job description for details on the essential criteria required for this role.

- WELSH LANGUAGE -
The ability to communicate and work through the medium of Welsh is essential for this post.

Digital Services Support Specialist (Carmarthen)

Carmarthen

Job Ref
51753
Location
Carmarthen
Salary
£26,707 - £30,378 per annum *
Closing Date
Monday, September 7, 2026

- THE ROLE -

The Digital Services Support Specialist is the first point of contact for all in-person digital service enquiries, delivering an exceptional, inclusive, and user-focused experience to students, staff, and visitors.
This role combines technical troubleshooting with outstanding customer support, ensuring seamless access to digital resources, systems and learning spaces.
The post holder will provide practical support and clear guidance across multiple channels, mainly face-to-face, by phone, and live chat, while accurately logging and managing requests through the Service Management platform. They will diagnose and resolve issues, triage complex queries, and escalate where necessary, ensuring to maintain timely and effective service delivery.

The role will actively promote digital services support and resources, maintain learning spaces and equipment, and manage short-term device loans and specialist resources. A Digital Services Support Specialist contributes to continuous improvement by collecting service data, creating knowledge base content, and identifying opportunities to enhance the user experience.
As this is a user-focused role, it requires strong interpersonal skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently while supporting team collaboration. By combining problem-solving expertise with proactive engagement, it plays a vital role in ensuring that all users can confidently access and benefit from the university’s digital services.

Please refer to the job description for details on the essential criteria required for this role.
